title: Client-aware degradation: request criticality scoring, dynamic admission, and cross-region failover
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: During high global load (notably cross-region failover windows) we observe correlated tail latency spikes and partial availability. Currently the runtime applies coarse tenant token-bucket admission and static priority lanes which sometimes evict mid-priority critical traffic. This ticket proposes a client-aware, SLO-driven load-shedding system that ranks requests by criticality, applies dynamic admission control and circuit-breaking policies per criticality band, and integrates cross-region fallback routing and graceful degradation modes. Goals: 1) keep SLOs for P99 latency and availability for "critical" requests (payments, auth, admin APIs) across failover events; 2) maximize successful completion for non-critical requests without blocking critical traffic; 3) provide predictable cost/behavior trade-offs and observability for rollouts.

acceptance_criteria: Critical requests (tagged or scored >= 0.85) retain target SLOs: p99 latency < 200ms and availability >= 99.9% during canary traffic profile.
Fallback rate for non-critical requests is documented and controlled (configurable target: <= 20% during peak control windows).
Circuit-breaker metrics emit events to the Console (per-tenant, per-criticality) and are visible in rollout dashboard.
Canary rollout automation implements automatic rollback if error budget burn > 5% in 30 minutes for critical band.
Integrations: existing Dedicated and Private deployments honor the same admission hooks via agent configuration.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Lab: unit tests, local simulator and deterministic scenarios (done)
Phase 1 - Canary (runtime-1.20): 2% production traffic in us-west-2, only synthetic failover windows simulated, monitor 48h
Phase 2 - Controlled regional expansion: add eu-west-1 with 5% traffic, enable cross-region routing for non-critical fallback
Phase 3 - Full: global rollout with per-tenant opt-in, default policy enforced for new tenants
Rollback plan: instant config toggles to disable scoring + revert to token-bucket-only admission; emergency fallback to per-tenant hard caps.
testing_plan: Automated unit tests for scoring hook and admission decisions
Integration tests: multi-region simulator with synthetic network partitions and region drains
Chaos experiments: random failover injection + sustained high tail queries from 10% of tenants
Load tests: calibrate token-bucket sizes and circuit-break thresholds using replayed production traces
User acceptance: run with 5 pilot customers requesting opt-in and collect qualitative failure-mode feedback
metrics: fallback rate (percentage of requests served by degraded mode) by region and tenant
circuit-breaker trip rate and recovery time
error budget burn and SLO projection (windowed)
decisions: Use a fast deterministic scoring function for criticality as step 1; defer heavy ML scoring to a follow-up (opt-in) feature to avoid operational complexity.
Admission control will be hierarchical: per-tenant hard cap -> per-criticality token bucket -> global soft admission with shedding percentages pulled from SLO policy engine.

Degradation modes (in order): 1) prefix/KV cache short-circuit, 2) reduced compute model variant (quantized/cheaper model), 3) async callback / queued completion, 4) explicit error with suggested retry-after. The controller will prefer cheaper models over error where latency impact is acceptable.

Cross-region fallback will prefer routing non-critical traffic to lowest-cost healthy region; critical traffic is pinned to primary and fails closed to avoid inconsistent side effects for stateful operations.
Expose per-tenant knobs in Console but keep safe defaults to prevent misconfiguration by non-admin users.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Risk: scoring mistakes could misclassify critical traffic -> mitigated by conservative thresholding and gradual opt-in.
Tradeoff: favoring cheaper model variants increases unit error rate for non-critical requests; we accept a small quality regression for cost/availability trade-offs.
Risk: added complexity in routing and observability; will invest in dashboards and playbooks before wide rollout.
Operational cost: additional cross-region egress may increase billing; implement cost accounting per-tenant and opt-in fallback to limit unexpected spend.
